A higher car insurance deductible can lower your bill. But first, do this quick break-even math that takes ten seconds. Your deductible is what you pay out of pocket on a claim before insurance pays the rest of the repair. Choosing a higher deductible, like one thousand dollars instead of five hundred, usually lowers your premium for collision and comprehensive. Here is the break-even test. Divide the extra risk you take on by how much you save each year. Say one thousand saves you two hundred a year. The extra five hundred of risk pays off after two and a half claim-free years. If you rarely file claims, a higher deductible often wins over time. And the savings repeat every single year. The catch: you need that deductible amount sitting in savings. If a surprise repair would put you in debt, stay lower. Run these numbers with your own insurance quote. Then follow for the next one: what renters insurance actually covers.
